IINVSYS Sales OS v2 · Sales → Delivery → Installation & Customer Service

User Manual

Everything the application does, screen by screen — including the pop-ups it opens, the alerts it raises, and every message it shows you when something is wrong.

About this manual

IINVSYS runs three linked processes in one system. A lead becomes a sale; a sale becomes a Work Order; a delivered Work Order becomes an Installation Job. You never create the downstream records by hand — the system creates them at the handoff points, and this manual shows where.

Two ideas explain almost every screen:

  • Gates block, flags don't. A stage gate is a list of conditions that must be true before a record moves forward; the server enforces it and refuses the move if they are not met. A hygiene flag is a data-quality warning — it never stops you working, it just puts the record on the review queue.
  • You only see what you may do. Buttons, menu entries and whole pages appear according to the permissions attached to your role. If a control described here is missing for you, your role does not hold that permission (see Appendix C).

Screenshots were taken against a working system with live data. Names, PO numbers and figures in the images are demonstration data.

The manual is always one click away: Manual ↗ at the foot of the sidebar, in every role.

1. Signing in

Open the application URL and sign in with your email address and password. On success you land on the Leads board.

When sign-in fails

The banner tells you which thing went wrong, and each case needs a different response.

Two more banners can appear here: ⚠ The server returned an error. Try again shortly. (the system is up but faulted — report it) and ⚠ Sign-in failed. (an unexpected condition).

Sessions and signing out

Your session lives in the browser tab. Closing the tab ends it; reloading the page keeps it. Use ⏻ Logout at the foot of the sidebar to end it deliberately — this also clears the data cached in the browser, so the next person to sign in on that machine sees nothing of yours.

2. Referrer invitations

Expo referrers do not get a password from anyone. A manager invites them, and the invitation link lets the referrer choose a password that nobody else — including the manager who sent it — ever knows. The link works once and expires.

3. Getting around

The sidebar is the whole navigation. It shows only the areas your role can open, along with your name, your role, the alert bell and the logout button.

The same screen, seen by different roles

Why a page might be missing. Menu entries are driven by permissions, not by job titles. “Delivery” appears for anyone with workorder.read, “Alerts” for anyone with notification.read, and so on. Appendix C lists exactly what each role holds.

4. The lead pipeline

Leads shows every open lead as a card in its stage column. Column names, colours and order come from the server, so they always match the current process definition.

  • Click a card to open the stage-gate drawer for that lead (§9).
  • Click “Details” on the card to open the full lead record (§6).
  • There is deliberately no drag-and-drop between columns: a stage change must go through its gate, so it happens in the drawer.

5. Creating a lead

+ New Lead opens a dialog. It appears for anyone holding lead.write.

Closing a dialog. Every dialog in the application closes with Esc, with its own Cancel/Close button, or by clicking the dimmed area outside it. Keyboard focus is held inside the dialog while it is open and returned to where you were when it closes.

6. Working a lead

The lead record is one screen: the edit form on the left, the stage history on the right, then documents and SPENCO scoring below.

What is validated when you save

Saving rejects values that are wrong, never values that are merely missing. A blank field flags the record for review; a malformed one is refused.

FieldRuleMessage
Contact namemust not be emptyName is required
Phone10-digit Indian mobile, starting 6–9A 10-digit Indian mobile (A7)
Emaila valid address, or blankNot a valid email
Deal valuezero or moreDeal value cannot be negative

Fields that exist for a reason

  • Designation — the exact job title, not “manager”. Required to leave Suspect.
  • State — the zone is derived from it; an unrecognised state raises a “Zone underivable” flag.
  • Competitor — required from Engagement onward; choose None Known if that is the truth. Choosing Other (specify) reveals a Competitor name box, which the gate also requires.
  • Next action — a specific action with an owner and a date, not “follow up”.
  • Products — these become the Work Order's line items at handoff. A sale closed with no products produces an empty Work Order, and Delivery's first gate cannot then be passed.
  • Commercial order (PO number, Subscription offered, AMC offered) — the Commercial Order gate reads these. AMC is mandatory for industrial company types.
  • If lost (lost reason, lost to, name, detail) — the Order Lost gate reads these.

Hygiene flags on a record

7. SPENCO qualification

SPENCO is scored at Prospect and gates the move to Engagement. Score each of the six dimensions from 0 to 5. The panel adds them up as you go; the server recalculates and stores the verdict when you save.

Two conditions must both hold: the total must reach the minimum (18 out of 30 by default) and every per-dimension floor must be cleared (Evidence of Need ≥ 3, Size ≥ 2 by default). Both are configurable in Settings, and the panel re-renders with the new rule immediately.

Press Save scoring to store the scores; a green Saved. confirms. The running total shown before saving is a preview of the server's arithmetic, not an input.

8. Documents

Documents are not decoration — two sales gates read this list. Negotiation requires a proposal or quotation on file; Commercial Order requires the customer's purchase order. Until then the panel says “Nothing on file yet — the proposal/quotation gate reads this list.”

Accepted file types are PDF, JPEG, PNG, WebP, HEIC, XLSX, DOCX, CSV and plain text, up to 15 MB. A file whose contents do not match its claimed type is refused — the message appears in the banner above the list.

9. Advancing a stage

Clicking a card on the board — or Advance stage → on the record — opens the gate drawer on the right. It names the move it is about to make and lists every requirement with [x] for met and [ ] for unmet. The list comes from the server, which is the same authority that will judge the attempt.

Overriding a sales gate

An override is permanent and attributed. The transition is recorded with your name, the note you typed, and the list of requirements that were waived. It shows in red on the record's history and in the audit log.
If the server refuses after you press Advance — because someone else changed the record, or a rule changed while the drawer was open — the drawer shows the server's own list of failures in red and the record is left untouched. Nothing partial is ever written.

10. Stage history

11. Review queue

Review queue is the manager's worklist of records with data-quality problems. The buttons across the top are the issue types, each with a count; clicking one filters the list to that issue, and clicking it again clears the filter.

What the flags mean

FlagMeaning
No company typeCompany Type is empty — it drives segmentation and the AMC rule.
No industry segmentIndustry is empty on a B2B contact.
No email (B2B)A business contact with no email address.
No designationThe exact job title is missing.
No state / Zone underivableState is blank, or is not one the zone map recognises.
Phone not a 10-digit mobileThe number does not match the Indian mobile format.
No expected close date / Close date in the pastThe forecast date is missing or stale.
No follow-up date / Follow-up date passedAn open deal with no future follow-up.
Follow-up >14d out, no reasonA distant follow-up with nothing recorded to justify it.
No next actionNothing specific is planned on the deal.
Inactive 30+ daysNo activity for the configured inactivity window.
Too long at stageThe deal has exceeded the maximum days for its stage.
No note this weekDeals at Engagement and above need a note every week.
Probability override unexplainedProbability was moved away from the stage default without a reason.

12. The delivery board

A Work Order is created automatically the moment a lead reaches Commercial Order. Nobody creates one by hand.

13. Working an order

The action panels appear only when they apply, in the order the process runs:

  1. Accept Work Order — the Delivery Manager takes ownership. Until this is done the order is flagged as unaccepted by the SLA sweep.
  2. Commit date — pick the target delivery date and record how the customer acknowledged it. This must happen within one business day of acceptance.
  3. Record delay — appears once a date is committed. A reason code and a revised date are both compulsory.
  4. Document vault — packing list, delivery note, tax invoice, the signed delivery acknowledgement and its photo evidence.
  5. Progression — Advance stage →, Dispatch (carrier or vehicle required) and Mark delivered (DA gate).

Two gate requirements are satisfied from this screen rather than by a separate save, and only if the move succeeds: the stock confirmation tick box (shown at Procurement) and the packing checklist sign-off name (shown at Preparation & Packing).

14. Marking delivered

Mark delivered (DA gate) closes the delivery. It is the one action with its own gate, separate from the stage gates.

15. The installation board

16. Running a job

Planning

At the Planning stage a Plan the job panel appears for users holding install.assign: technician name, scheduled date, and the name of the person at the customer who confirmed site readiness. Save it before advancing.

Checklists

Snags

Commissioning

Handover and the support window

Record the trained attendees (comma separated) and press Record handover. That starts the support window: a proactive check-in falls due seven days later, and support issues logged here carry a 48-hour resolution SLA. A breached issue is shown in red as [open · SLA BREACH].

17. Feedback and closure

A job cannot close without customer feedback. Record the CSAT score (0–5) and any comments.

18. Alerts

Alerts are raised by the system, not by people. They are addressed by permission, so you see the ones you are able to act on.

What the system will tell you about

EventSeverityRaised when
handoff.workorder_createdcriticalA sale reached Commercial Order and a Work Order now awaits acceptance.
handoff.installation_createdcriticalA delivery was completed and an Installation Job was created.
delivery.date_unconfirmedcriticalA Work Order is unaccepted past the 1-business-day SLA, or accepted with no committed date.
delivery.delay_loggedwarningA delivery date was revised.
lead.inactivecriticalAn open lead has had no activity for the inactivity window (30 days by default).
lead.notes_stalewarningA deal at Engagement or above has had no note this week.
install.commissioning_failedcriticalA commissioning test was recorded as failed.
install.handover_completeinfoA job was handed over; the support window has started.
install.issue_sla_breachedcriticalA support issue passed its 48-hour resolution SLA.
install.csat_lowcriticalFeedback came back below the CSAT escalation threshold.
install.corrective_action_overduecriticalThe corrective action plan for a low-CSAT job is past its due date.

Sweeps run on a schedule (sales hygiene and inactivity early each morning, installation clocks shortly after, delivery SLA clocks hourly through the working day, all Asia/Kolkata). Repeat alerts for the same record are suppressed for a cooling-off period, so a stale record does not spam you daily.

19. Dashboard & export

  • Last full month / Month to date switch the window.
  • All / Sales / Delivery / Installation narrow the page to one process (Figure 19.3).
  • ⤓ Export xlsx downloads the workbook for the selected window, named IINVSYS-report-YYYY-MM-DD.xlsx.
  • Hygiene queues at the foot count the records needing attention, in amber when non-zero.

20. Admin

Admin holds the three reference lists. Agents and Expos may be edited by managers and above; Products by superadmins only. Lower roles see the tables without the add, edit or delete controls.

Delete asks for confirmation in a browser dialog that names the record — Delete “IINVSYS Pro”? — and removes it only if you accept. There is no undo on this screen.

21. Settings

Settings holds the rules that the source process documents left open. A change takes effect immediately, with no restart, and invalidates every browser's cached gate checklist so nobody keeps validating against the old rule.

RuleControls
SPENCO minimum totalThe score out of 30 needed to leave Prospect.
SPENCO per-dimension minimumsHard floors that apply in addition to the total.
Company types requiring AMCThe working definition of “industrial” for the AMC rule at Commercial Order.
Competitor mandatory from stageThe stage from which a competitor must be named.
Probability override toleranceHow far probability may move from the stage default before it is flagged.
Delay clock resets on re-revisionWhether the 48-hour delay notice is measured against the original or the latest committed date.
State → Zone mappingWhich state belongs to which zone.
Inactivity alert (days)Days without activity before a lead is flagged.
Follow-up horizon (days)How far ahead a follow-up may be set before it needs a reason.
Note staleness (days)How often deals at Engagement and above need a note.

Sales

ProspectDesignation · Company · Company type · City · State · Industry and Email (B2B contacts) · Next action · a future follow-up date.
EngagementSPENCO scored and qualifying · Competitor named (and named in full if “Other”) · Deal value · Product/package · a future expected close date · a future follow-up date.
NegotiationA proposal or quotation on file · a current expected close date · a future follow-up date · Next action.
Commercial OrderThe customer PO uploaded · PO number · Deal value matching the PO · Subscription offered or already active · AMC offered or already active for industrial company types · an expected close date.

EnteringRequires

Scheduling & DispatchPacking list, delivery note and tax invoice attached · packing checklist signed off.

Installation & Customer Service — no override

EnteringRequires
Installation PlanningNothing — the job is created here.

Post-Installation SupportSigned handover certificate uploaded · trained attendees recorded · handover checklist complete.

Appendix D — Confirmations and browser prompts

Two actions use the browser's own dialog rather than an in-page one, so they look different depending on your browser and cannot be screenshotted from inside the application:

WhereDialogEffect
Admin → any table → DeleteA confirmation reading Delete “<name>”?Accept and the record is deleted; cancel and nothing happens. There is no undo.
Installation job → Sign checklistA prompt reading Technician name signing this checklist:The name you type is recorded as the signature. Cancelling, or leaving it empty, signs nothing.

Everything else — New Lead, Add/Edit in Admin, and the stage-gate drawer — is an in-page dialog that traps keyboard focus, closes on Esc, and returns focus where you left it.

Appendix E — Known limitations

  • Installation technician assignment. The planning panel records a technician's name for reporting, but the On-Site gate requires a linked user account, and the application currently offers no way to pick one. Until that is added, that requirement can only be satisfied by an administrator through the API, and the panel says so on screen.
  • No override outside sales. Delivery and installation gates cannot be forced by anyone. If a gate is genuinely wrong for your business, change the rule in Settings rather than looking for a way around it.
  • Sessions are per tab. Closing the tab signs you out; there is no “remember me”.

End of manual.
